Hi Elena —

Appreciate the questionnaire, and looping in Soojin (our security engineer) and Ben (solutions) to provide the detailed answers. High-level summary up front so your review team has immediate context:

- Residency: Customer-hosted API requests for Arcadian can be routed to our EU-only tenant (primary in eu-west-1) and we can apply a geofence configuration so data is stored only in EU regions unless you request otherwise.
- Retention: Default behavior for hosted API requests is to retain request metadata (headers, timestamps, usage metrics) for 365 days and full request/response payloads for 14 days to support debugging. We offer an opt-in extended retention tier (subject to contract) where full transcripts are retained up to 90 days for troubleshooting and analytics.
- Deletion: We provide an on-demand purge API and a console-driven erasure workflow. Typical erasure propagation to live storage and indexing completes within 48 hours; backups and snapshot propagation occurs per the backup retention lifecycle (see Soojin's note below for timing).
- Backups & DR: Automated encrypted backups are retained for 180 days; snapshots used for DR are rotated on a 30–90 day cadence depending on configuration. All backups are AES-256 encrypted and access-controlled via KMS.
- Training: We do not use hosted API request content for model training or to improve models unless a customer explicitly opts in via a contract amendment.

Soojin will add the technical specifics, including KMS key handling, S3 lifecycle behaviour, and legal hold exceptions. I’ve attached our one-page Data Handling summary for quick reference.

Next steps: we can (1) populate the attached questionnaire directly, (2) schedule a 30‑minute technical review with your security team, or (3) produce an evidence bundle (configs + screenshots + signed DPA). Which do you prefer?

Thanks,

Hi Elena — Jordan asked me to respond with the operational details. I’ve included line-by-line answers for sections 4–7 from your questionnaire and called out implementation notes and evidence files.

SECTION 4 — Data residency
- Storage location: For Arcadian we will provision an EU-only tenant (primary region eu-west-1). Customer object storage and indexed request data are stored in S3 buckets that are region-locked to eu-west-1. Cross-region replication is not enabled by default; if you require multi-region DR we can enable replication to eu-central-1 under a separate configuration and contractual addendum.
- Network boundary: All control-plane traffic for the tenant is routed over our private VPC peering in the configured region; customer data plane traffic terminates on instances in the same region.

SECTION 5 — Retention and logical deletion
- Types + default retention (hosted API):
  • Request metadata (headers, latency, token counts): 365 days (used for billing/analytics).
  • Full request+response payloads: 14 days (default) — this is stored encrypted at rest and used only for debugging and investigative support tickets.
  • KV cache and prefix caches: ephemeral TTL configurable per-customer; default 6 hours. Cached contents are not persisted to long-term backups by default.
  • Embeddings/indexed vectors: persisted per-customer index and retained per your configured retention window; default 90 days for ephemeral indexes unless you have a dedicated index with a longer SLA.
  • Aggregated telemetry and usage metrics: retained 2 years for product analytics (no PII).

- Opt-in & contractual variants: We offer an extended retention plan (up to 90 days for full transcripts) and a strict-ephemeral mode (full transcripts retained 0–24 hours) — both are contract options set at onboarding.

SECTION 6 — Deletion / Erasure workflows
- Erasure mechanisms: (1) console-driven account erasure (self-service), (2) purge API for programmatic deletes, and (3) support ticket for manual assistance.
- SLA & propagation windows: Live-store deletion completes within 48 hours. Backup/snapshot purge follows a staged process: snapshot markers are flagged immediately and content is irretrievable within 7 days; full physical removal from rotated backup media completes within 30–90 days depending on snapshot cycle.
- Evidence & isolation: When an erasure request completes we generate an audit record (timestamp, requestor, objects touched). We can provide redacted manifests as evidence during vendor reviews.

SECTION 7 — Backup, encryption & access controls
- Encryption: Data at rest uses AES-256; keys are managed via customer-scoped KMS keys when requested (customer-managed CMKs available on Dedicated / Private but we can bind a per-tenant KMS in the Hosted EU tenant under an addendum).
- Backups & retention: Automated backups retained 180 days by default; backup snapshots are rotated and immutable for the configured retention window.
- Access controls & human access: Access to plaintext data is restricted to a small, audited SRE/security on-call group and requires MFA + short-lived elevated access with just-in-time approval. All such accesses generate audit logs retained 365 days.

ADDITIONAL NOTES
- Training & research: We do not include hosted API request data in model training unless you sign an opt-in training consent. If opted in, training datasets are explicitly scoped, documented, and available for review.
- Legal hold: Legal holds override normal deletion rules. If an export/legal hold is required, we will advise on the expected retention and provide a manifest.

EVIDENCE (attached)
- s3-lifecycle-policy.png — sample lifecycle rules showing snapshot/expiry markers.
- kms-key-policy.txt — redacted KMS policy example for a per-tenant CMK.

If helpful I can (a) fill the spreadsheet responses directly, (b) schedule a tech call with our infra team to walk through the S3 lifecycle diagrams, or (c) prepare a short evidence bundle (screenshot + signed statement) you can attach to your vendor pack.
